newsitem.title: UK: US stocks mixed in London, awaiting sales data.
newsitem.headline: US stocks mixed in London, awaiting sales data.

text.p: U.S. shares were mixed in London in thin trading on Tuesday as investors awaited U.S. sales figures and a slew of corporate results, dealers said.
"Trading is spotty, but it feels like the market is ready to consolidate a bit more," said one London dealer.
European investors, they added, were awaiting the 1230 GMT release of June retail sales data. The report is expected to show sales rose 0.2 percent last month.
Most technology shares were slightly firmer, with Intel Corp adding $1/4 to $79 ahead of its results today.
According to First Call, the chipmaker was expected to report second quarter profits of $1.80 per share, up from $1.17 per share in the year ago period.

Activity in London also centred on Boeing Co shares, which retreated after the European Commission said concessions offered by Boeing to win EU approval for its proposed merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp were not good enough to alleviate concerns about the effects on competition.

The shares were down $1/4 to $56-7/8, having earlier climbed $1/4, after the Financial Times said the U.S. aircraft giant was close to reaching an agreement with the European Commission on Boeing's proposed merger with dealers said.
The EU said the deadline for Boeing to make offers on the merger deal is today.
Dealers also noted selling in DuPont Co shares in the wake of the company's $3 billion purchase of Imperial Chemical Industries Plc's chemical operations.
Elsewhere, shares in International Paper Co eased $1/4 to $59-1/2 on profit-taking after a surge in recent weeks, dealers said.
In other trading, September S&P 500 futures were trading 1.25 points lower on Globex at 925.60. September long bond futures were off 8/32 to 113-22/32.
